name: Joel
overview: Joel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as the firstborn son of Samuel. His lineage places him within the Levitical priestly tradition, and he is noted specifically for his familial connection rather than any independent narrative or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Joel means "y-h-v-h is God [El]," reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the sovereignty of the LORD. This proper name is recorded in Scripture without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Joel is explicitly recorded as the son of Samuel, making him part of a significant prophetic family. Additionally, he is inferred to be the son of Heman, connecting him to a notable Levitical lineage. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Joel's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily tied to his identity as the firstborn son of Samuel, a major prophetic figure. This connection situates him within the Levitical heritage and the early prophetic ministry in Israel. His mention underscores the continuation of priestly and prophetic service through Samuel's family line.
